bindings.explanation: REQ-6-3-4 says a Request changes decision blocks merging only until that reviewer re-decides for the current compare commit, or the compare branch gains a new commit that makes the old decision stale; REQ-6-5 therefore forbids merging only when a *valid* Request changes exists. The real merge gate mergeBlocked delegates to hasRequestChanges, which keeps the last decision per reviewer without ever comparing review.commitId to the current compare head, so a Request changes recorded on an earlier compare commit blocks forever. Fixture (unchanged from the run, which failed on the stale assertion): seeded Open PR p1 (repo r1, base main, compare feature-search) whose compare head is commit c2, reviewed by the seeded non-author Write collaborator bob-reviewer; r1's protection rule is cleared in setup so the target is the unprotected scenario REQ-6-5 explicitly defines as having 'no additional approval-count or check-success requirement' while still requiring 'no valid Request changes review', making the stale decision the only possible blocker. The control pins the same decision to c2 and is still blocked, proving the predicate is live; after a compliant repair the stale case has no other blocker and must return null.

bindings.subject: mergeBlocked
bindings.requirement_text: From the Files changed link, the reviewer activates the Review changes button to open one review form with an optional Summary field, radio controls named Comment, Approve, and Request changes, and a Submit review button. Selecting Approve and submitting without a summary is valid and displays Approved. Selecting Request changes with a summary displays Changes requested and that exact summary; the decision remains visible after reload. Seed data supplies a non-author Write reviewer and separate Open PRs for approval and request-changes submission, with no initial effective decision by that reviewer. A user who is not the PR author and has Write, Maintain, or Admin may submit Comment, Approve, or Request changes on an Open PR; the author and Draft PRs cannot submit reviews. The system stores the review decision, reviewer, current compare commit, optional explanation, and time; a new decision by the same reviewer replaces that reviewer's effective decision for the current commit while preserving the old record. Approve is valid only when the reviewer is not the author and the compare commit is still the same; Request changes blocks merging until that reviewer submits a new Comment or Approve for the current compare commit, or the compare branch receives a new commit that makes the old decision stale. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-1 (View Pull Request Overview and Commits) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

bindings.explanation: REQ-6-2-2 requires the creation entry to be disabled when base and compare are the same branch *or* when there is no difference (no comparable commits), and REQ-6-2-3 forbids creating a PR record in that case. The real comparison observer compareScreen only disables creation when the two branch *names* are equal, so two distinct seeded branches that point at the same commit (r1 'release' and r1 'draft-feature', both at c1) render an enabled Create pull request entry, and the real creation handler createPull then persists an Open PR with an empty changed-file set for that pair. Fixture: seeded contributor bob-reviewer (Write grant g2 on public repo r1); the pair release→draft-feature has no existing Open/Draft PR, and the control pair main→feature-search has real differences. The check invokes the real handler with the ctx shape the compare form passes (dataset carrying base/compare, form carrying title/body), so it exercises the transition instead of filtering state itself.

bindings.subject: compareScreen
bindings.requirement_text:
The PR comparison page is a read-only page shown before creation: base is the target branch that receives the merge result, and compare is the source branch that provides the changes to merge. A user with Write, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner status clicks “New pull request” on the “Pull requests” page and selects the two branches; the system calculates comparable commits, changed files, and a diff summary based on the commits they currently point to. If the branches are the same or there is no difference, the creation entry is disabled; comparison does not save a PR, commit, or branch change. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-3-1 (List and Switch Repository Branches) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. Only signed-in users with Write, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner status may compare branches on the repository pull-request page; Read and Triage may view existing PRs but cannot enter the creation-comparison flow. The system validates the role and rejects unauthorized requests. New pull request is a link. The comparison page has native select controls with combobox roles named base and compare; each option's visible label is its exact branch name. Compare changes is a button. For a valid selection it displays the known changed file path verbatim, a Commit summary with the comparable commit count, and an enabled Create pull request button. Selecting the same branch in both fields immediately displays No changes and disables the creation button, without requiring Compare changes to be clicked first. Clicking Compare changes retains that result. Seed data supplies a contributor with Write permission, a public repository PR-list page entry, a base branch, a distinct compare branch ahead by at least one commit, and a known changed file. Separate valid comparison page entrys open the same usable creation flow with the branches already selected; these pairs have no existing Open or Draft PR at the start of each creation scenario.

The seeded changed-file path for comparison is `src/search.ts`.

![image](reference/github-compare-branches.png)

bindings.explanation: REQ-6-5 states the startup state supplies an eligible Open pull request (targeting protected main, non-author approval, test success) *and separate Open pull requests for the success and refusal scenarios*, the refusal PR being an Open PR on a protected branch that lacks the required valid approval and is explained by 'Review required by branch protection'. This is a startup-coverage claim, so the check derives both roles from the real predicate mergeBlocked over the actual seeded collections (adding the missing records is exactly what a compliant repair may do) instead of pinning counts; the preconditions only establish that the executor can read the real startup data (signed-out visitor, seeded org repository r1 with its protected main rule) and do not assert the missing condition. Execution shows the eligible branch holds (p1) while no distinct Open, approval-blocked PR exists for the refusal scenario, so the refusal scenario has no restorable seed state.

bindings.subject: mergeBlocked
bindings.requirement_text: On an eligible PR, Merge pull request and then Confirm merge are buttons; confirming displays Merged, and that state remains after reload. A blocked PR keeps a visible disabled Merge pull request button and explains its unmet review or protection condition before any click. Seed data supplies a Maintain account and separate Open PRs for success and refusal. The eligible PR targets protected main, has a current non-author approval and test: success, and has no conflicts. The blocked PR targets a protected branch and lacks the required valid approval; its disabled button is accompanied by Review required by branch protection. Each seed state is restored independently before reuse. “Merge” is the only write operation that writes the current compare commit's changes from an Open PR into the base branch; it is not simply marking the PR as complete. Only Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may merge from the PR detail page using the sole supported “Create a merge commit” method; the merge confirmation area should display satisfied and unsatisfied conditions. Before confirmation, the system rereads the target branch head, current compare commit, merge-conflict state, and protection rules — there must be no valid Request changes; if the target is protected, each enabled rule requirement is enforced independently, requiring 1 valid non-author Approve for the current compare commit when Require 1 approval is enabled and requiring `test` success when Require status check test is enabled. An unprotected target has no additional approval-count or check-success requirement, but merging still requires no merge conflicts and no valid Request changes review. After validation succeeds, the system atomically creates a merge commit whose parents are the target-branch head at merge time and the current compare commit, updates the target-branch head, sets the PR to Merged, and stores the merger, time, and resulting commit identifier. If any condition is unsatisfied or persistence fails, the page explains the applicable reason and neither the target branch nor PR changes; a missing required approval displays “Review required by branch protection”. Merged is terminal. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-4 (Submit a Pull Request Review) and REQ-6-1 (Protect Branches with Review and Status-Check Requirements); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

bindings.explanation: REQ-6-6 requires the PR page to provide 'Close pull request' as a button for authorized users and states that the author (or Maintain, Admin, organization Owner) may close an unmerged Open *or Draft* PR without merging. The real page builder prScreen instead renders 'Reopen pull request' for a Draft (and lets that control put the Draft straight into Open), so the seeded Draft PR authored by the signed-in author offers no way to close it. Fixture: seeded PR p3 (repo r1, number 3, author alice-dev, state Draft, branch pair main←draft-feature) observed as its own author alice-dev, who is also the seeded organization Owner and therefore explicitly authorized by REQ-6-6; the control uses the seeded Open PR p1 by the same author, whose page does render 'Close pull request', proving the binding and the page composition are live.

bindings.subject: prScreen
bindings.requirement_text: The PR page provides Close pull request and Reopen pull request as buttons for authorized users. Close pull request immediately sets Closed without an extra confirmation dialog, then Reopen pull request immediately restores Open. After reload, Close pull request is available again. For a viewer who is neither author nor Maintain/Admin/Owner, both controls are absent, rather than merely disabled or rejected after activation. Seed data supplies the author and a separate Read viewer, an authored Open PR for the close/reopen cycle, and a separate Open PR readable by that viewer for permission validation. When the proposed change should not proceed, the PR author, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may close an unmerged Open or Draft PR without merging; the same roles may reopen a Closed PR as Open. The system stores the status, operator, and time and records the transition, while keeping the PR discussion, reviews, diff, and branch references viewable; closing or reopening must not update any branch. Merged is terminal, the page does not display close or reopen operations, and the server rejects status changes. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-2-3 (Create a Pull Request from Comparison Results) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.
